faq_plan.q: What is a sermon evaluation form?
How do I create a sermon evaluation form?

plan.angle: The top 10 is printable sheets and preaching advice (a search-committee sheet from 2007, seminary PDFs, a Logos sermon sheet, the Keller and 9Marks forms, a blog worksheet): each gives one listener a page of questions and stops there. None shows what happens to five filled-in sheets after Sunday. This page covers the sermon evaluation form as an app: listeners score the sermon on a phone, the app averages each area, keeps the comments with the scores, sends the preacher one summary and tracks each area week over week.
tab_stories: Stillwater Creek Church has a 5-person feedback team that scores each Sunday sermon 1 to 5 on text, main idea, application and delivery before Monday noon; the app averages the five, and application is the lowest area this week at 2.8.

At Northgate Seminary, 9 classmates and Professor Ostrander score each student sermon in the preaching lab; the student, Hannah Voss, sees the class average next to the professor's own scores, kept in separate columns.

First Avenue Fellowship's 7-member pastoral search committee watches one recorded sermon from each of 3 candidates and scores all three on the same form, so the averages sit side by side and candidate B leads on handling the text at 4.6.

Harvest Lane Church scores a 10-week series on Philippians, and the average for 'the main idea was clear' climbs from 3.1 in week 1 to 4.2 in week 10 after Pastor Gil Sorensen starts stating the point in one sentence.
